problem: Improve a small classifier on sklearn.load_digits (1797 handwritten8x8 digit images) under label-preserving corruptions: additive pixel noise and random pixel dropout. Use fixed stratified train/validation/test split, fit preprocessing on train only, reserve test for final evaluation, and compare a standardized RBF-SVM plus ordinary corruption augmentation. Optimize mean accuracy across clean and fixed corruption severities under 5 CPU minutes on an Apple Silicon laptop, no pretrained models or external data. Propose a distinct implementable intervention and ablation; do not merely list known techniques or claim external novelty.

proposal.title: Arc-Sampled Joint Corruption Augmentation for RBF-SVM on Digits
proposal.intervention: Generate augmented training samples by sampling a mixing angle θ uniformly from [0, π/2] per sample, then applying additive Gaussian noise with σ = β·cos(θ) and pixel dropout with rate p = β·sin(θ), where β=0.25 is a fixed corruption budget. This constrains every augmented sample to lie on a quarter-circle in (σ, p) space, ensuring the full joint corruption manifold is covered rather than only its axes. Fit a StandardScaler on clean training data only, apply it to augmented training and all evaluation sets, then train an RBF-SVM (C=10, gamma='scale') on the augmented set.
proposal.mechanism: Ordinary augmentation applies noise and dropout independently or separately, leaving the interior of the joint corruption space underrepresented during training. By enforcing cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, every augmented sample has identical L2 corruption energy but a different noise-dropout composition. The SVM decision boundary therefore encounters interpolated corruption mixtures during training, which should reduce accuracy degradation on mixed-corruption test conditions without inflating the total augmented set size beyond practical SVM training time.
proposal.assumptions: Test corruptions remain within the β budget. The arc parameterization provides meaningfully denser interior coverage than independent sampling at equivalent sample counts. SVM generalization improves from distributional coverage rather than mere sample count inflation. Clean-only scaler fitting correctly normalizes corrupted inputs because corruption is zero-mean.
proposal.baseline: Same RBF-SVM (C=10, gamma='scale') trained on augmentation that applies noise and dropout independently at fixed σ=β and p=β, matched for total augmented sample count, with identical scaler and split.
proposal.metric: Mean classification accuracy averaged across six fixed test conditions: clean, low noise, high noise, low dropout, high dropout, and mixed noise-plus-dropout, all evaluated on the held-out test set.
proposal.falsification: Train four models with identical augmented sample counts: clean-only resampled, noise-axis-only, dropout-axis-only, and arc-sampled braided. If braided accuracy on the mixed-corruption condition does not exceed both axis-only models, the benefit is attributable to sample count rather than joint-space coverage, falsifying the core mechanism.
proposal.implementation: Normalize raw pixels to [0,1]. Stratified splits: 15% test, 15% of remainder validation, rest train. Apply braided_augment with n_copies=4 to training data only. Fit StandardScaler on clean training pixels. Transform augmented train, validation, and each corruption-specific test set. Fit SVC(kernel='rbf', C=10, gamma='scale'). Report per-condition and mean accuracy. Total wall time expected under two minutes on Apple Silicon.
